## Part 1: Read and Inspect

```{r}
plots <- read.csv("plot_survey.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
str(plots)
```

The data contain `r nrow(plots)` rows and `r ncol(plots)` columns. The `canopy` column has an unexpected character type: the text entry `not recorded` prevents R from recognizing the column as numeric.

## Part 2: Clean It

First, make the invalid canopy text an explicit missing value and convert the measurements to numeric. There are `r sum(plots$canopy == "not recorded")` such canopy entries to convert.

```{r}
canopy_missing <- plots$canopy == "not recorded"
plots$canopy[canopy_missing] <- NA
plots$canopy <- as.numeric(plots$canopy)
```

The biomass value `r -999` is a sentinel for an invalid measurement, not a real negative biomass, so I converted `r sum(plots$biomass == -999)` such values to missing values.

```{r}
biomass_sentinel <- plots$biomass == -999
plots$biomass[biomass_sentinel] <- NA
```

`soil_ph` already uses `NA` for missing measurements. I kept those missing values as missing rather than imputing or dropping plots; `r sum(is.na(plots$soil_ph))` plots have missing soil pH.

```{r}
# Confirm the cleaned measurement types and missing-value counts.
str(plots)
colSums(is.na(plots))
```

## Part 3: Summarize

The summaries below use the cleaned measurements. Base R's `na.rm = TRUE` excludes unavailable measurements from each calculation.

```{r}
biomass_mean <- mean(plots$biomass, na.rm = TRUE)
biomass_sd <- sd(plots$biomass, na.rm = TRUE)
canopy_mean <- mean(plots$canopy, na.rm = TRUE)
canopy_sd <- sd(plots$canopy, na.rm = TRUE)

site_counts <- table(plots$site)
treatment_counts <- table(plots$treatment)
biomass_by_site <- tapply(plots$biomass, plots$site, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
missing_soil_ph <- sum(is.na(plots$soil_ph))

biomass_mean
biomass_sd
canopy_mean
canopy_sd
site_counts
treatment_counts
biomass_by_site
missing_soil_ph
```

After cleaning, mean biomass is `r round(biomass_mean, 2)` (SD `r round(biomass_sd, 2)`), and mean canopy cover is `r round(canopy_mean, 2)` (SD `r round(canopy_sd, 2)`). Site counts are: ridge `r site_counts[["ridge"]]`, riparian `r site_counts[["riparian"]]`, and valley `r site_counts[["valley"]]`; treatment counts are: control `r treatment_counts[["control"]]` and thinned `r treatment_counts[["thinned"]]`. Mean biomass by site is ridge `r round(biomass_by_site[["ridge"]], 2)`, riparian `r round(biomass_by_site[["riparian"]], 2)`, and valley `r round(biomass_by_site[["valley"]], 2)`. There are `r missing_soil_ph` plots with missing `soil_ph`.

## Part 4: Answer a Question

I used logical subsetting to compare thinned plots at riparian and ridge sites.

```{r}
thinned_riparian <- plots$biomass[
  plots$treatment == "thinned" & plots$site == "riparian"
]
thinned_ridge <- plots$biomass[
  plots$treatment == "thinned" & plots$site == "ridge"
]

mean_riparian_thinned <- mean(thinned_riparian, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_ridge_thinned <- mean(thinned_ridge, na.rm = TRUE)
difference <- mean_riparian_thinned - mean_ridge_thinned
mean_riparian_thinned
mean_ridge_thinned
difference
```

Among thinned plots, mean biomass is `r if (difference > 0) "higher" else "not higher"` on riparian sites than on ridge sites by `r round(abs(difference), 2)` biomass units.

## Part 5: Make One Figure

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Biomass by canopy cover"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
plot(
  plots$canopy,
  plots$biomass,
  xlab = "Canopy cover (%)",
  ylab = "Biomass (recorded units; unit not specified)",
  pch = 19,
  col = "darkgreen"
)
```

The figure shows the observed relationship between canopy cover and biomass for plots with both measurements recorded.
